text: The first whole-cell computational model (Karr et al., 2012, Science) simulated which organism, and why was this organism chosen?
choices: Escherichia coli, chosen because of its extensively curated genome-scale metabolic model
Mycoplasma genitalium, the smallest known self-replicating organism (525 genes), whose small genome made comprehensive integration of cellular submodels tractable
Saccharomyces cerevisiae, chosen as the simplest eukaryotic model organism
Mycoplasma genitalium, chosen because it was the first organism to have its genome sequenced
explanation: Karr et al. modeled Mycoplasma genitalium specifically because, as the smallest known free-living, self-replicating organism (525 genes), its limited complexity made it feasible to integrate 28 submodels covering its cellular processes -- a task that still took 128 person-years. E. coli (choice 0) is a much larger, more complex organism used instead for more limited ME-models, not the first whole-cell model, and yeast (choice 2) is a eukaryote not discussed in this context. Choice 3 names the correct organism but the wrong justification -- genome sequencing order was not the reason it was chosen.
